label: Early original-phase step shortly after j/u/n/g input
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase at early positions (t=1..4; peak t=2-3, almost nothing after t=6) when one of the letters j, u, n, or g (weaker: v) was input one or two steps earlier. Strongest when the previous input is j/u/n (lift ~5.6-5.9x) and when such tokens are stacked (e.g. j j 2 reaches max); activation decays over the next 1-2 steps after the trigger. Almost silent at t=0, at the delimiter (1.4% of mass), and in the copy phase. Low-magnitude misses are diffuse early-position activations without a j/u/n/g trigger, or later positions (t=5-6); false positives are mostly g triggers or triggers at t=4.

issues: Reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.796, R 0.807, F1 0.802, mass recall 0.903. Most of the missed activations are weak: coverage in the lowest activation quartile is 0.47, and in the top two quartiles it is 0.96 and 0.99.

The factual claims check out on dev. The t=0 rate is 0.000. Activation mass by position peaks at t=2 (0.346) and t=3 (0.309) and is about 0 from t=7 on. Delimiter mass is 0.014 and copy mass is 0.001. Lift when the previous token is j, u or n is 5.9x, 5.6x and 5.6x. g is weaker (3.9x) and v weaker still (2.1x).

The feature is graded, not a hard gate. When the trigger is the previous token, precision falls with position: 0.97 at t=1, 0.96 at t=2, 0.94 at t=3, 0.67 at t=4 and 0.21 at t=5. When the trigger is only two steps back, precision is about 0.71 at t=2-3 and 0.48 at t=4. This decay matches the stated 'fades' and 't=4 false positives' caveats, and I found no hidden modulator: precision at t=4 does not change with L or with how many triggers came earlier (0.66-0.68 throughout).

Minor residual: when the previous token is v or f at t=2-3, with no j/u/n/g trigger, the feature fires with precision 0.39 and recall 0.055. Adding v to the predicate raises recall to 0.844 but lowers F1 to 0.794, and adding f lowers it to 0.774. So this is not worth including.
Minor residual: the delimiter step right after a trigger (short L) fires with precision 0.45 but recall 0.013. Including the delimiter step changes test F1 to 0.798, which is no gain.

None of the alternative predicates I tried beat the original. Two other variants scored F1 0.784 (dev) and 0.798 (test). The original predicate looks like a local optimum, and no systematic counterexample class remains.
